raw_plan.root_cause: The return value of atoi is used directly as an index into a 16-byte stack buffer at [rbp-0x20] without any upper-bound check; only a negative check (js) is performed, so any index >= 16 writes past the buffer.
raw_plan.original_behavior: Calls atoi on the input string, stores the result; if the result is non-negative, writes byte 0x58 to dst[index] where dst is a 16-byte buffer at [rbp-0x20], then calls puts with the string at 0x402004; if negative, does nothing. No upper bound is enforced, so index >= 16 causes an out-of-bounds stack write.
raw_plan.required_invariant: The index used for the write must satisfy 0 <= index <= 15 (capacity-1) so that the write stays within the 16-byte buffer; out-of-range indices must be rejected without performing the write.
raw_plan.repair_strategy: After atoi, check the result against both bounds: reject if negative (as before) and reject if greater than 15. Only when 0 <= index <= 15 perform the byte write to dst[index] and the puts call; otherwise skip both, preserving the original control flow for valid inputs.
raw_plan.failure_behavior: For out-of-range indices (negative or >= 16), skip the out-of-bounds write and skip the puts call, then return normally (matching the original negative-index path).
raw_plan.expected_behavior: For valid indices 0..15, write 0x58 to dst[index] and call puts(0x402004), identical to the original. For indices < 0 or > 15, perform no write and no puts call, returning cleanly without memory corruption.
verification_conditions: Input index in [0,15] produces the same observable output as the original (puts called, byte written at dst[index]).
Input index < 0 performs no write and no puts call.
Input index >= 16 performs no write and no puts call; no bytes outside [rbp-0x20, rbp-0x10) are modified.
Function terminates with ret and preserves SysV x86_64 calling convention.
Only direct calls to 0x401060 (puts) and 0x401080 (atoi) are emitted; no other calls, syscalls, or indirect jumps.

note: baseline is deterministic; AI target assembly is accepted only by native/qemu PoC+regression. baseline_target_strict calls repair_any(target=<case target>, require_target=True) and records the resolved target_scope plus target_in_scope (every produced action inside the target; empty action lists are not in scope). baseline_target_aware receives the same target/capacity hint; ai_blind uses the public AI path without target. allow_calls only permits direct calls already present in the target function.
